\noindent\scriptsize Each \AC\ pair is selected-flow/helicity-summed then all-flow/fixed-helicity; \PAC\ SymJIT O1 uses matching pruned and shared artifacts.  Entries are generation seconds above runtime wall microseconds per point; \PAC-only cells are absolute. Green/orange/red means below one/below two/at least two.  Summaries are \texttt{min|max|avg|med|sum}; \texttt{sum} compares paired totals. \texttt{>30 GB RAM} marks only the affected selected/all-flow workload. A \textbf{VALIDATION FAILED} marker means the same-point difference exceeds \(10^{-8}\).
\par\vspace{0.15em}
\paragraph{Settings.}
\noindent\scriptsize \path{docs/result_matrix.py} (\texttt{--color-accuracy lc}) writes this table and its JSON cache. \AC\ uses its generated library for the selected workload and the fixed-helicity \texttt{imode=2} colour probe for all flows. \PAC\ writes separate \texttt{selected\_flow} and shared \texttt{all\_flows} artifacts. \PAC\ uses Rusticol double precision; selected/all-flow batches are 128/64.  Selected JIT stages measure chunks around base 128; all-flow outputs use uniform chunk 8192.  Stage-local inputs, ten Horner iterations, default CPE rounds, expanded optimization limits, SymJIT O1, and \texttt{--target-runtime 10} are used. The two LC workloads are displayed side by side.
\par\vspace{0.15em}
\paragraph{Runtime interpretation.}
\noindent\scriptsize On AArch64, Rusticol runs saved SymJIT stages as native two-lane complex evaluators and packs each stage input once across its chunks.  Wall time measures the public \texttt{evaluate} call; the profiler separates evaluator and packing work.  Low-multiplicity fixed overhead can dominate an \AC\ call measured in nanoseconds.  Ratios at or above two are reviewed throughout, with \(n\geq5\) as the scaling gate.

\end{landscape}
